findings.text: Filesystem lookup service resolves a type by its base name ignoring any suffix after a dot, attempts on demand loading when absent, and returns a referenced object or null when unavailable or when a subtype suffix is supplied for a type without subtype support.
Lookup of a registered filesystem occurs under read side protection and success pins the owning module. Failure to pin is treated as absence.

Writeback request descriptor combines a page budget and target superblock with a sync mode and initiation reason, completion signalling for waiters, linkage for pending queues, and single bit selectors for tagged, kupdate, cyclic, background, full sync and self releasing behaviour.
Default lazy timestamp expiry interval equals 43200 seconds corresponding to twelve hours.

Foreign writeback detection uses a thirteen bit time scale where one second equals 8192 units, averaging with one eighth weight for new samples, cutoff divisor eight, and a two second evaluation period.
Foreign history keeps sixteen slots per inode with unit derived from period divided by sixteen, activation threshold at eight slots and maximum considered run at five slots.
Concurrent foreign queueing is bounded at 1024 entries to avoid excessive buildup.
Each writeback switch context fits within roughly one kilobyte after header, capacity expressed as remaining bytes divided by pointer size.

Inode to writeback binding selects a memory cgroup aware target when that mode is active using either folio or task context, otherwise the default device target, installing the result exactly once under contention.
Concurrent attach attempts for the same inode have a single winner. Losers release their extra reference.
Switch batch carries queue linkage for pending batches plus a trailing null terminated collection of inode references that guarantees paired completion of a two phase move.

Per inode ownership transfer moves reclaimable and writeback accounting plus list membership from old to new target, refreshes dirty timing, clears foreign detection state and marks completion, while freeing or retiring inodes are left untouched.

Ownership transfer holds the inode lock together with exclusive page cache protection and relies on an ordering barrier before clearing the switching flag so observers seeing the cleared flag also see the new target.

Batch migration serializes against concurrent sync issuance with a read semaphore and acquires the two writeback list locks in address order with nesting annotation, dropping and reacquiring them when scheduling is needed mid batch.

Switch work drains all queued batches for a target after a grace period that makes the switching mark visible, holds a protective reference across the drain, wakes the new target when any inode moved, and releases inode, cgroup, batch and counter resources afterward.
Batch preparation walks a writeback list from the aged end toward the front, rotating examined entries to preserve expiry order and stopping one slot before capacity to retain space for termination.

Offline cleanup migrates attached and timestamp only dirty inodes toward the nearest available ancestor cgroup target, falling back to the device default when no ancestor target can be created, and reports whether further passes are required.
Helper for direct data flush binds an inode to its writeback target under its own lock before attaching it to the supplied control structure.

Targeted flush by device and memory cgroup identifiers looks up both objects without creating a missing writeback context, estimates dirty volume with a one quarter margin over current file dirty count, and queues a non blocking cyclic request that self releases.
Targeted flush reports absence when device, cgroup or writeback lookup fails and reports memory exhaustion when the request descriptor cannot be allocated.
Early initialization creates a per processor workqueue dedicated to writeback switching and reports memory exhaustion on failure.
Background initiation only wakes the flusher thread, leaving actual background work to occur when no higher priority work remains.
Superblock writeback membership tracking is idempotent with double checked list state, adding on first mark and removing on first clear.
Superblock membership updates use interrupt saving protection on the superblock writeback list lock while the outer emptiness test remains lock free.

Dirtied recency compares stored dirty time against a cutoff, with an additional guard on short word builds that discards future appearing timestamps caused by wraparound of constantly redirtied inodes.

Expiry migration drains aged entries from the tail until a recent entry is found, tags each moved inode as queued for sync, and regroups the result by superblock when more than one ordinary filesystem is present while leaving the special block device collection ungrouped.
Predicate identifies the shared block device superblock when block support is enabled, otherwise never matches.

Dispatch preparation merges deferred work, then pulls expired entries from both dirty and timestamp only lists using a shorter deadline for timestamp entries except during full sync, signalling when any inode became eligible.
Dispatch preparation requires the writeback list lock to be held by the caller.
Waiting for in progress inode sync must release the inode lock while sleeping and reevaluate the sync flag that was sampled under that lock to ensure ordering.

Post writeback disposition distinguishes freeing inodes that are ignored, skipped pages that cause delayed requeue, residual dirty pages that either requeue for another slice or delay on blocking, metadata only dirtiness, timestamp only dirtiness returning to its dedicated list, and fully clean inodes returning to the attached set.
Full sync and tagged passes refresh dirty timing on still dirty inodes to prevent repeated selection within the same pass.
Two requeue helpers exist. One delays an inode to the tail under its own lock and one moves it to the intermediate more work list assuming the caller already synchronizes list access.

Per invocation page budget is unbounded for full sync or tagged passes to allow single pass completion, otherwise limited by the smaller of half recent bandwidth or a share of the global dirty limit and the remaining work budget, rounded to filesystem preferred granularity.
Switching membership concurrently with superblock wide sync risks the sync missing the moving inode unless migration holds shared protection against that path.
Writeback trace event definitions are instantiated in this compilation unit.
Number of switch batches in flight is tracked by an atomic counter and processing is serialized through a dedicated workqueue created at init.
